name: euler-column-pinned-quad8
reference: Benchmark B5: Euler buckling of a pinned-pinned column, E = 210 GPa, nu = 0.3, 20 x 1000 mm with a plane-stress thickness of 10 mm. I = t b^3 / 12 = 6.6667e-9 m^4, so P_cr = pi^2 EI / L^2 = 13817.45 N against the 1 MPa reference pressure on the 20 x 10 mm end (P_ref = 200 N): lambda = 69.0872, gated at 1 %. Plane stress rather than a solid on purpose: a solid column pinned on a line is free to spin about its own axis, which is a rigid mode, not a buckling mode. Modelled as the lower half by symmetry, 20 x 500 mm: the pinned end is ux = 0 across the y = 0 edge, which holds the section laterally while leaving it free to rotate, and the mid-height plane is uy = 0, which is the symmetry condition of the sin(pi y / L) fundamental mode. Fixing uy on the end edge instead would clamp the section and give the fixed-pinned load. The closed form neglects shear: with L/b = 50 the Timoshenko correction puts pi^2 EI / L^2 about 0.10 % above the exact critical load, so the computed value is expected to sit just below the reference.

checks.note: P_cr = pi^2 EI / L^2 over the 200 N reference load
